newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian c.bank to monitor foreign investments.
newsitem.headline: Croatian c.bank to monitor foreign investments.

text.p: Croatia's central bank will start monitoring foreign direct and portfolio investments in the country in a more systematic manner, the bank said in a statement on Wednesday.

"All legal entities in which foreign institutions have stakes of any kind and those who have holdings abroad are required to report all foreign investments made until the end of 1996 by the end of March," the bank said.
It said systematic monitoring was necessary for a more complete survey of the country's balance of payments.
Branches of foreign institutions who do business in Croatia and foreign firms owned by Croatian companies are also required to report their investments.
The regulation will be also applied to businessmen with permanent residence in other countries and Croatian citizens holding work permits abroad.
From next year, annual investment reports will have to be made by the end of February, the statement said. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
